title: VA Home Loan Guaranty Funding Fee Exemption Arising from a Compensation Award
content:
Holding a compensation award changes the funding fee on a VA Home Loan Guaranty loan.

## Who is exempt for a loan

A veteran is exempt for a loan when, on its closing date, the veteran was receiving compensation, was entitled to compensation but receiving retired or active-duty pay instead, had a pre-discharge or proposed rating, or was an active-duty Purple Heart recipient. These grounds are those of the program's exemption list.

## A later award

A veteran who paid the fee and is later awarded compensation becomes exempt for that loan when the award is effective on or before the closing date.

## Correcting the exemption on the loan

The exemption on a loan is corrected only when the veteran's compensation award shows an effective date of service connection on or before the loan's closing date. The authority is the system record: the veteran's compensation award and the loan record of the particular loan whose exemption is corrected. A compensation award effective after the closing date never makes an earlier loan exempt, and a pending claim is not enough.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

| Effective date of service connection on the veteran's award, against the loan's closing date | Exemption on that loan corrected |
|---|---|
| The day before the closing date | Yes |
| The closing date itself | Yes (on or before includes the closing date) |
| The day after the closing date | No |
| No award; a claim is pending | No |

## Points of judgement

- **One award, several loans.** The comparison is made loan by loan: an award effective on a given date can reach a loan that closed on or after that date, and never a loan that closed before it.
- **What the veteran says versus what the record shows.** The effective date that counts is the one the compensation award shows; a pending claim is not enough.
